title: Computer Networks
standfirst: How the Internet actually works — layered protocols, routing, transport, and the design principles behind them.
resources_note: An IITM email may be required for some of the resources above; any other access request will be strictly rejected.

description_paragraphs: This course introduces the architecture and operation of computer networks using a top-down approach, examining how applications communicate over the Internet and how data is transmitted reliably, efficiently, and securely across layers.
faculty: Prof. Ayon Chakraborty, Department of Computer Science and Engineering, IIT Madras

weeks_text.label: Week 1
weeks_text.text: Introduction to computer networking; Internet architecture and design principles.

weeks_text.label: Week 2
weeks_text.text: Layered protocol stack; Packet structure and network analysis tools.

weeks_text.label: Week 3
weeks_text.text: Network performance fundamentals; Delay, throughput, and latency metrics.

weeks_text.label: Week 4
weeks_text.text: Quality of Experience (QoE); Web performance measurement techniques.

weeks_text.label: Week 5
weeks_text.text: Socket programming basics; Client-server communication models.

weeks_text.label: Week 6
weeks_text.text: Application-layer protocols; TCP traffic analysis and behavior.

weeks_text.label: Week 7
weeks_text.text: Reliable data transfer; Transport layer protocols and mechanisms.

weeks_text.label: Week 8
weeks_text.text: Flow control; Sliding window protocols in TCP .

weeks_text.label: Week 9
weeks_text.text: Congestion control algorithms; TCP fairness and optimization.

weeks_text.label: Week 10
weeks_text.text: IP addressing and subnetting; Routing fundamentals.

weeks_text.label: Week 12
weeks_text.text: Medium access control (MAC); Wireless communication protocols.
